hook: Content note: the middle of this file is a casualty list of violent deaths written in clinical, explicit detail. Around it sits a sharper idea: an abandoned amusement park held by a sniper perimeter, where the signal to evacuate is simply hearing music. The containment section is the part to read closely, since it is built around sound and shifting zones rather than a creature.
whyItMatters: The cause is never described; the file defines it entirely through its aftermath and the perimeter drawn around it. The contrast between bright theme-park branding and flat bureaucratic language carries most of the effect. It also stages internal Foundation friction in miniature, with field requests for escalation answered by brief refusals from above.
thingsToNotice: The source of the effect is only ever the "artifact in question", which keeps attention on the colored zones and the realignment events after each burst of music. The three addenda at the end are short memos, a refused airstrike, a measured expansion and a refused reclassification, and they read as a quiet argument between people on site and people far away. The cheerful ride names are chosen on purpose; the distance between those names and the record attached to them is where the dread comes from.
